# Halyard Weekly — 2026-09-08

> Source: authored fixture transcript (task-701.01, synthetic). Participants: Tanya Team, Tina Team, Xavier Expert.

# Halyard Weekly
2026-09-08

**Tanya Team:** Morning, both. Let's keep this one tight — I want to come out of it with the cutover shape actually decided, because the steering group asks again on Thursday and I've given them "we're still working it" twice now.

**Tina Team:** Morning.

**Xavier Expert:** Morning. I've got the replica numbers, whenever you want them.

**Tanya Team:** Hold those for ten minutes. Sequencing first. Tina, you've been living in the site plan — where are we?

**Tina Team:** Four sites. Northgate, Dockside, Ferry Road, and Clyde. Northgate is the smallest and the cleanest, Clyde is the one nobody wants to touch.

**Tanya Team:** And the question on the table is whether we take them together or one at a time.

**Tina Team:** That's the question.

**Tanya Team:** Then let me say where I've landed, because I don't think I'm going to move off it. We do this one site at a time. A site goes live, it soaks, and only when that soak is clean do we start the next one. No parallel cutovers, not even for the two small ones.

**Tina Team:** I'm with you on that.

**Xavier Expert:** Can I push on it for a second? Not because I disagree — because the steering group will push and I'd rather they push here.

**Tanya Team:** Please.

**Xavier Expert:** The argument for taking Northgate and Ferry Road together is that they share a dispatch desk. If you split them, the desk runs two systems for however long the soak is, and that's the thing the desk supervisor has been shouting about since June.

**Tanya Team:** It is. And I've thought about it, and I still think it's the wrong trade. Running two systems at one desk for a few weeks is a known, contained pain with a named owner. Two cutovers landing in the same week is an unbounded one, and we've got nobody to hand it to.

**Xavier Expert:** That's a fair answer. I'd put it to them exactly that way — contained versus unbounded.

**Tina Team:** And the desk supervisor's pain is a rota problem, which is solvable. A double cutover is a staffing problem and a data problem at the same time, which isn't.

**Tanya Team:** Right. So: one at a time, with a soak.

**Tina Team:** Agreed, and I want to put a number on the soak, because "a soak" without a number turns into three days the first time someone's under pressure. The soak is two full weeks. That's the Dockside number, and I'd hold us to it.

**Tanya Team:** Say more about where two weeks comes from.

**Tina Team:** Dockside pilot, back in the spring. We watched the exception queue after go-live and it didn't flatten out until day nine or ten. Two weeks gives you the flattening plus a few days to actually look at what flattened. Anything less and you're starting the next site while you're still finding out what the last one did.

**Tanya Team:** That's the reasoning I wanted on the record. Two weeks, from the Dockside exception curve.

**Xavier Expert:** I'll note that the exception curve is the only evidence we have for it. It's one site, one season.

**Tina Team:** It's one site, one season, and it's the only site we've actually done. I'd rather hold two weeks and shorten it with evidence than hold one week and discover we needed two.

**Tanya Team:** Agreed. Xavier, replica numbers.

**Xavier Expert:** Right. During a cutover window the live system is under load it has never seen — the migration job, the dual-write, and whatever the site is actually doing that day. Reporting on top of that is what took Dockside down for forty minutes.

**Tanya Team:** I remember the forty minutes.

**Xavier Expert:** So the position I want us to take is: during cutover, every reporting read comes off the replica. Not "should", not "where possible" — reporting does not touch the live system during a cutover window, full stop.

**Tanya Team:** Does that cost us anything real?

**Xavier Expert:** Replica lag. Somewhere between thirty seconds and four minutes depending on the migration job. So a reporting number can be four minutes stale during a cutover. My argument is that a four-minute-stale number is fine and an outage is not.

**Tina Team:** Nobody is making a decision off a four-minute-old parcel count at two in the morning.

**Xavier Expert:** That's my view too.

**Tanya Team:** Then that's the rule. Reporting reads come off the replica during cutover. Xavier, write it into the runbook as a rule and not as guidance, because guidance gets negotiated at three a.m.

**Xavier Expert:** Will do.

**Tanya Team:** Last one. Reference data.

**Xavier Expert:** This is the one I keep going round on. The vendor holds the reference tables — carrier codes, service levels, the zone map. We can take a copy at any point. The question is when we become the system of record for them.

**Tanya Team:** And your view?

**Xavier Expert:** The vendor stays the system of record for reference data until the last site is live. Every site reads from the vendor's copy, we mirror it read-only, and we take ownership on the day Clyde goes green and not a day earlier.

**Tanya Team:** Because?

**Xavier Expert:** Because if we take ownership at site one, we've got two sites on our reference data and two on theirs, and the zone map drifts between them. You find that out from a mis-priced consignment three weeks later. Keeping one source of truth through the whole programme is worth more than getting ownership early.

**Tanya Team:** I agree with that, and I'd add: it also means the vendor can't tell the steering group that their reference data was fine and ours broke it. Their data, their problem, right up until the end.

**Xavier Expert:** That's the other half of it, yes.

**Tina Team:** No objection from me. It's less work for the site teams too.

**Tanya Team:** Good. So Thursday I'm telling them: one site at a time, two-week soak between sites, reporting off the replica during cutover, vendor holds reference data until Clyde is green. Anything I've mangled?

**Tina Team:** That's it.

**Xavier Expert:** That's it.

**Tanya Team:** Thanks both.

payload.rationale: This Halyard Weekly transcript is a fixture demonstrating the product's core thesis: a structured meeting that produces persistent decision records with reasoning and attribution. I expanded the foundational narratives (DecisionsEvaporate, DecisionCaptureAtConsensus) and the core feature position because the document is an instance of capturing decisions at consensus with full context — Tanya explicitly says 'That's the reasoning I wanted on the record.' The AntiSlackPositioning narrative and AntiPatternRealtimeChat position frame the anti-pattern this document stands against. Sprint4ThesisProven and ContextPreservationNextSprint are included because the document exemplifies the thesis proven in Sprint 4 and demonstrates context preservation (linking decisions to the discussion that produced them). StyleObs_Sprint4_DirectQuote is included because the document uses the same direct-quote-from-named-participants style. ProductCategoryAsyncPlatform defines the category this document instantiates. I deliberately did NOT expand pricing positions (PricingTier25Plus, PricingTwelveDollars), webhook architecture, Zephyr integration, or target market — none overlap with the cutover sequencing, replica reporting, or reference data decisions in this document.

positions.name: SiteCutoverSequencingStrategy
positions.frame: how should multi-site cutovers be sequenced when operational containment conflicts with local site friction?
positions.why: Weighs the trade-off between bounded, contained operational friction (running dual systems at a shared desk) versus unbounded risk (attempting parallel site cutovers with shared staffing).

positions.name: PostGoLiveSoakDurationBasis
positions.frame: how is the minimum soak duration between site cutovers determined and validated?
positions.why: Grounds the two-week soak policy in historical exception-queue stabilization data from the Dockside pilot, balancing empirical caution against pressure to shorten timelines.

positions.name: CutoverReportingReadIsolation
positions.frame: how are reporting workloads isolated from production systems during high-load cutover windows?
positions.why: Establishes a mandatory runbook rule isolating production instances by offloading all reporting queries to replicas during cutovers, trading minor query latency for outage prevention.

positions.name: ReferenceDataSourceOfRecordTransition
positions.frame: at what milestone in a multi-site rollout should reference data authority transfer from vendor to internal systems?
positions.why: Determines that vendor reference data remains the single system of record throughout the entire migration programme until the final site (Clyde) goes live, preventing configuration drift.

placements.why: The discussion articulates overarching governance principles and strict operational boundaries for managing a phased technical migration across multiple sites.
placements.title: operational containment and governance rules for multi-site rollouts
placements.frame: How does the organization structure, sequence, and isolate technical and operational risks during multi-site system cutovers?

placements.title: known, contained operational friction is prioritized over unbounded parallel cutover risk

placements.why: Establishes a firm sequencing thesis: sites cut over strictly one at a time with a mandatory two-week soak grounded in exception queue flattening, accepting contained local friction to avoid unbounded multi-site failure.

placements.title: reporting workloads are strictly isolated to replicas during high-load cutovers

placements.why: Establishes an absolute operational rule in the runbook requiring all analytical and reporting reads to hit read replicas during cutover windows to prevent live system outages.

placements.title: vendor remains the authoritative system of record until full programme cutover

placements.why: Establishes the policy that reference data ownership remains with the vendor until the final site cutover completes, avoiding multi-site drift and clear accountability boundaries.
